newsitem.title: UK: Abtrust European moves to active management.
newsitem.headline: Abtrust European moves to active management.

text.p: Abtrust European Index Investment Trust plc said on Thursday it planned to move to an active management investment policy and gain exposure to European small and mid-cap companies.

In a statement, it said its passive management policy, pursued since February 1993, had met the objective of matching growth in the FTSE Eurotrack 100. Prior to February 1993, it had been actively managed.
It said a move to active management should enable it to significantly outperform this index, "particularly through exposure to European small and mid-cap companies".

"The investment policy will now replicate the Abtrust European Fund, a unit trust whose strong track record must be clear evidence of the company's future investment potential," chairman David Thomson said.
From February 1993 to end-February 1997, the trust's net asset value rose 53.9 percent, which it said was disappointing compared with other European trusts.
Over the same period, unit trust Abtrust European Fund's net asset value rose 98.9 percent.
The statement said the 42.5 million sterling Abtrust European Index Investment Trust planned a name change to Aberdeen European Investment Trust.
